questions.question: HTML5 provides validation via attributes such as:

options.text: required, min, max, minlength, maxlength, pattern, type

questions.explanation: Native constraints: required, min/max (numbers/dates), minlength/maxlength, pattern (regex), and type-based checks (email/url).

questions.question: The :invalid CSS pseudo-class targets:

options.text: Inputs whose current value fails a constraint

questions.explanation: :invalid styles fields that currently violate a constraint (e.g. empty required). Pair with :valid for feedback UI.

questions.question: To show a custom validation message you use the Constraint Validation API:
questions.explanation: setCustomValidity('') clears (valid); a non-empty string marks invalid and reportValidity() shows the bubble.

questions.question: The 'pattern' attribute uses:

options.text: A JavaScript-style regular expression the value must match

questions.explanation: pattern holds a RegExp (anchored automatically); it's evaluated against the value during validation. Add title for guidance.

questions.question: novalidate on a <form> does what?

options.text: Disables native browser validation for that form

questions.explanation: novalidate turns off built-in validation — useful when you handle validation entirely in JS.

questions.question: An edge case with pattern: the regex is implicitly:

options.text: Anchored (must match the whole value), so ^ and $ are not needed

questions.explanation: HTML pattern validation anchors the regex to the full value; you don't add ^...$. A partial match fails.

questions.question: In Angular Reactive Forms, validators like Validators.email are set:

options.text: In the FormControl/FormGroup definition (component), not the template

questions.explanation: Reactive Forms define Validators in TS (e.g. this.fb.group({email:[null, Validators.email]})), keeping logic in code.

questions.question: Best practice: validate on BOTH client and server because:

options.text: Client validation is for UX; server validation is the authoritative security check
Server validation is slower so skip it
Only one layer is ever needed

questions.explanation: Client-side gives instant feedback; server-side is mandatory because client checks are bypassable.
